contracting.h1: One contract, from empty shell to open doors.
contracting.lede: You hand over a space and a brief. We hand back a finished, tested, authority-approved environment — with a single team answerable for every trade in between.

offer.title: The whole build, under one signature
paras: Splitting a fit-out across a designer, a main contractor, an MEP subcontractor and an AV specialist means four programmes, four invoices and four versions of whose fault it is.

Turnkey contracting removes that. We take responsibility for design coordination, procurement, construction, services, finishes and commissioning — and for the sequence that holds them together. One programme, one cost plan, one project lead who answers the phone.

We work across residential villas and apartments, offices and clinics, retail and F&B units, and hospitality spaces. Scope can be fixed-price against a detailed bill of quantities, or open-book where the design is still moving.

faq.q: Can you work in an occupied building?
faq.a: Yes. We regularly phase works or run out-of-hours programmes in occupied offices, retail units and residential buildings, coordinating with building management on access, noise windows and service isolations.

faq.q: Who handles the authority approvals?
faq.a: We do. Submissions, permits and NOCs are part of the Turnkey Complete and Design & Build Plus packages, and available as an add-on to Fit-Out Essential.

faq.q: Can you take over a project another contractor started?
faq.a: In most cases, yes — subject to a condition survey and a written record of what was completed and to what standard before we mobilise.

faq.q: Is the price fixed?
faq.a: Fixed-price against an agreed bill of quantities is our default. Where the design is still developing we can work open-book with an agreed management fee, converting to fixed price once drawings are frozen.

project-management.lede: We don't build it. We make sure it gets built — to your programme, to your budget and to the standard you were promised.

offer.title: A professional client-side team, without the headcount
paras: A contractor's job is to deliver their scope profitably. Somebody has to hold the whole programme, verify what's been paid for and say no when it matters. That is our role.

Innova acts as your representative from the moment there is a brief. We shape the scope, run the tender, administer the contract, monitor the programme and cost, inspect the quality and close the project out with a documented handover.
The engagement is deliberately independent: where we are project managing, we are not also the contractor. You get advice that isn't defending its own margin.

facility-management.h1: Buildings that keep working after everyone goes home.
facility-management.lede: Planned maintenance that prevents the call-out, and a response team for the times it still happens.

offer.title: Maintenance as a schedule, not a reaction
paras: Most property problems in this climate are predictable: AC performance, water systems, seals, electrical loads. They become expensive only when nobody is watching the schedule.

We build a maintenance regime around your actual assets — surveyed, listed and given a service interval — then run it to a calendar you can see. Reactive call-outs still happen, and we staff for them, but the aim is to make them rare.
We cover private villas and apartments, offices, clinics, retail units and mixed-use buildings, either as an annual contract or as part of a handover from one of our own construction projects.

cinema.h1: A room that disappears, so the film doesn't.
cinema.lede: Private cinemas, media rooms and multi-room audio — designed around acoustics and sightlines first, calibrated on completion, and serviced afterwards.

offer.title: The room matters more than the equipment
paras: Expensive speakers in an untreated room sound worse than modest speakers in a treated one. Most disappointing cinemas are a room problem wearing an equipment problem's clothes.

We start with the space: dimensions, reflections, seating distance, sightlines and where the noise is coming from. Only then do we specify equipment, and we specify it to suit the room rather than a price list.
Every installation is calibrated on completion — picture and sound measured and adjusted, not left at factory defaults — and handed over with a control system simple enough that guests can use it.

snagging.h1: Find it before you sign for it.
snagging.lede: An independent inspection of your property before handover. Every defect photographed, located and described in a report the developer can act on — and we come back to check they did.

offer.title: The last moment your leverage is free
paras: Once you accept handover, defects become a warranty claim: slower, more contested and sometimes at your cost. Before you accept, they are simply the developer's outstanding work.

A snagging inspection uses that window properly. We go through the property room by room against finishing standards, record every defect with a photograph and a location, grade it by severity, and issue a register formatted for the developer's own rectification process.
We are independent of the developer and the contractor. We are paid to find things.

faq.q: When should the inspection happen?
faq.a: Between the developer notifying you that the unit is ready and you signing the handover acceptance. That is the point at which outstanding work is still clearly the developer's obligation.

faq.q: What if the developer disputes the report?

faq.q: Can you snag a property that's already handed over?

marketing.lede: Positioning, campaigns and press relations built around what actually moves your commercial numbers — not around what fills a content calendar.

paras: A great deal of marketing spend goes into saying more, more often, about a proposition nobody has made clear. Volume rarely fixes that.

We begin with positioning: what you sell, who it is for, why it is different and what would have to be true for someone to believe it. That produces a messaging framework — and everything after it, from a website to a press release, gets easier and more consistent.

From there we run the visible work: content, social channels, campaigns, media relations and events. Reporting is against commercial metrics you actually care about — enquiries, qualified leads, cost per acquisition — rather than impressions.

consultancy.h1: Growth outruns process. We help it catch up.
consultancy.lede: Operating models, documented processes, governance and controls — built for the size you are becoming rather than the size you were.

offer.title: The company outgrew how it was run
paras: Most operational pain in a growing business is not a people problem. It is a structure problem: decisions with no owner, processes that live in someone's head, and reporting that arrives too late to act on.

We diagnose that structure honestly — through interviews, process mapping and a look at the actual numbers — and then rebuild the parts that are failing. Target operating model, documented procedures, delegation of authority, financial controls, performance measures.
Recommendations are only half the job. We stay through implementation, because an unimplemented report changes nothing.

ai.h1: Artificial intelligence, applied where it actually pays.
ai.lede: We start with your processes, not with a model. Where AI creates measurable value we build it. Where it doesn't, we say so.

offer.title: Most AI projects fail on the use case, not the technology
paras: The models are capable and getting more so. The failures we see are almost always upstream: a use case nobody needed, data that was never ready, or a pilot with no definition of success.

Our work begins with an assessment of where your organisation actually spends effort — the repetitive reading, writing, searching, checking and routing that consumes hours without producing judgement. Those are the places AI pays.

We then prioritise by value and feasibility, build one use case properly end-to-end, measure it against agreed success criteria, and only scale what earns it. Deployment includes the parts people skip: data governance, privacy, residency, evaluation and the training that gets it adopted.

faq.q: How do you measure whether a pilot worked?
faq.a: Against criteria agreed in writing before development begins — typically time saved, error rate, throughput or cost per transaction, measured against a documented baseline.

packages.note: Packages are a starting point, not a limit. Tell us how you use the property and we will shape the service around it.

steps.d: Tell us about the property and how often you are away. A conversation first, never an obligation.
We visit, record the property’s baseline condition and agree the visit routine with you.
Scheduled visits begin, each one documented with photographs and readings you receive the same day.
Anything found is flagged with a recommendation — and fixed by our own maintenance team on your approval.

faq.q: How quickly can visits start?
faq.a: Usually within a week of the walkthrough. Tell us your travel dates and we will schedule the first visit around them.

faq.q: Is this the same as a maintenance contract?
faq.a: It complements one. Maintenance keeps the systems serviced; Home Watch keeps eyes on the property between services — and the two are run by the same team, so nothing falls between them.

faq.q: Can you look after pets and plants?
faq.a: Yes. Pet feeding, plant watering and mail handling are part of the visit routine, on the schedule you set. We speak English, German and Arabic.

faq.q: What happens in an emergency?
faq.a: The visit team is backed by our 24/7 maintenance line. Anything affecting safety, security or habitability is escalated immediately and coordinated until it is resolved.

talk.title: Talk to us about Home Watch & Property Concierge
talk.p: Tell us where the property is and how you use it. We will come back with a visit routine and a written quote.
